chunks: Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (peace be upon him) said:

God said: 'O son of Adam! By My will you came into being as one who desires for himself whatever he desires; and by My strength you fulfilled My obligations; and by My favour I gave you the strength to disobey Me. I made you hearing, seeing, and strong.

Whatever good reaches you is from God, and whatever evil reaches you is from yourself — and that is because I have greater right to your good deeds than you do, and you bear greater responsibility for your evil deeds than I do.
And that is because I am not questioned about what I do, but they shall be questioned.'

key_terms.أَوْلَى: More worthy/having greater right — the comparative term establishing asymmetric responsibility
key_terms.حَسَنَة: Goodness/good deed — attributed to God as the ultimate source of all good
key_terms.سَيِّئَة: Evil/bad deed — attributed to the human self as the locus of wrongdoing
key_terms.فَرَائِض: Obligatory duties — the religious obligations God has enjoined upon His servants
key_terms.مَشِيئَة: Divine will/desire — the sovereign intent of God by which all existence is established
key_terms.مَعْصِيَة: Disobedience/sin — acts contrary to God's commands, for which humans bear full accountability

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Ridha report about divine will and human responsibility in this hadith qudsi?
ai.summary: This is a hadith qudsi (divine narration) in which God, through the words of Imam al-Ridha (AS), addresses humanity with a profound statement about divine will, human agency, and moral responsibility. God declares that human existence, capacities, and even the ability to choose are granted by God — yet when humans sin, the evil is attributed to themselves, not to God. The audience of the early Shia community would have understood this as a middle position between fatalism (jabr) and absolute free will (tafwid), affirming that God's sovereignty does not negate human accountability.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr who said, 
‘Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Said: “O son of Adam<sup>as</sup>!

By My<sup>azwj</sup> Desire you came into being. You desire for your own self whatever you so desire; and by My<sup>azwj</sup> Strength you are fulfilling My<sup>azwj</sup> Obligations, and by My<sup>azwj</sup> Favour I<sup>azwj</sup> Given you the Strength (so you may) disobey My<sup>azwj</sup>. I<sup>azwj</sup> Made you to be hearing, seeing, strong.

Whatever you attain from a goodness, so (it is) from Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and whatever you attain from evil, so it is from yourself, and that is because I<sup>azwj</sup> am closer with your good deeds than you are, and you are closer with your evil deeds than I<sup>azwj</sup> am,
and that I<sup>azwj</sup> will not be Questioned about what I<sup>azwj</sup> Do, but they would be questioned’.
en.sarwar: 6. It is narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn abu Nasr who has that Imam abul Hassan al-Rida has said the following. “

Allah said, ‘O son of Adam through My wish you came into existence and it is you who wish for yourself whatever you wish. Through My power you fulfill your obligations and through My bounties you receive strength to disobey Me. I made you made you to hear and see and be strong.
Whatever good you receive is from Allah and whatever evil afflicts you is from your own-self. It is because I have priority to your good deeds and you have priority to your bad deeds.
This is because I Ahmad ibn Muhammad not asked what I do but they are questioned ffor what they do.”
